newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-June 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-June 6.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- MING PAO -- A Democratic Party member successfuly obtained legal aid to challenge in court the legality of bills passed by the provisional legislature.
-- WEN WEI PO -- Beijing has set up a government image and strategy research committee to help improve the international image of the government, state organisations and their staff.

-- ECONOMIC TIMES -- All the top posts at the Xinhua News Agency Hong Kong branch may be replaced after the retirement of its present head, Zhou Nan, due to strained ties between the agency and Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa.
-- ECONOMIC TIMES -- The People's Bank of China has ordered all Chinese commercial banks and their branches to stay clear of the stock market in an effort to further cool surging bourses.
-- TIN TIN DAILY -- Taiwan independence and "pro-Japan, anti-mainland" concepts dominate new history textbooks in Taiwan, drawing attention from all sectors of the island.

-- SING TAO -- Gang wars in Macau have seriously damaged the businesses of gangs themselves, and some gangs are luring Hong Kong students looking for summer jobs on tours of the territory, detaining them, then demanding ransoms from parents by claiming their children lost money at the gambling table.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Diplomatic sources said Chinese President Jiang Zemin will attend Hong Kong's midnight handover ceremony on June 30 but is expected to return to Beijing at noon the next day for celebrations there.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- A major obstacle for Hutchison Whampoa in its protracted bid to win the port-handling contract at Subic Bay in the Philippines had been eliminated after four Philippine officials were cleared of any wrongdoing by the country's ombudsman.
